interest: Shows Consul Sokobin exposing Japan's Tsingtao 'military hospital' as cover for a division-sized permanent garrison in occupied Shandong.
overview: This file (State Department decimal 894.247, January–March 1939) documents U.S. diplomatic reporting on Japanese military construction activities in Tsingtao (Qingdao), China. American Consul Samuel Sokobin initially reported in January 1939 that the Japanese military was leveling land adjacent to the local golf course using hundreds of Chinese laborers for what was ostensibly a military hospital. By mid-March 1939, following a personal visit to the site, Sokobin observed that the immense scale of construction far exceeded a medical facility. Correlating his observations with an address in the Imperial Diet by the Japanese War Minister regarding the indefinite stationing of troops and barracks construction in China, Sokobin concluded that the Japanese were erecting a permanent army post designed to house thousands of troops or more than a full division. The file contains original telegrams, internal State Department paraphrases, and an administrative charge slip.
